lineage_context.teaching_goal: Exploit the project's ideal Halesia-vs-Styrax pair using buds, pith, shoot age, ovary position and fruit wings.

project_scope.selection_mode: Two-genus project module: Halesia diptera + Styrax platanifolius
project_scope.note: The two project taxa provide a nearly textbook genus comparison supported directly by Flora of North America.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: On a shrub or small tree with showy pendent white flowers, inspect the calyx/ovary junction and then the fruit. Styracaceae project members have partly to fully inferior ovaries and dry fruits.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Alternate simple exstipulate leaves; twigs and leaf surfaces often bear stellate hairs.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers bisexual, usually white, with fused corolla at least basally and 7–16 stamens; ovary partly to fully inferior depending on genus.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Dry, either nutlike/capsular or winged. The project genera split dramatically here.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Halesia vs Styrax is best learned as a five-character card: bud scales, pith, shoot age, ovary position, fruit wings.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: pendant flower → ovary position → bud/pith → fruit wings → genus card
visual_lesson.intro: This may be one of the best genus-comparison families in the whole learner because Halesia and Styrax differ in several visible characters that all reinforce each other.

steps.title: 1 · Halesia door: scaled bud + chambered pith
steps.look_for: Winter buds with scales and chambered pith.
steps.why_it_matters: Vegetative character pair that strongly favors Halesia.

steps.title: 2 · Halesia flower and fruit
steps.look_for: Four-lobed corolla, fully inferior ovary, then a conspicuously 2- or 4-winged dry fruit.
steps.why_it_matters: The winged fruit is an outstanding field confirmation.

steps.title: 3 · Styrax door: naked bud + continuous pith
steps.look_for: Winter buds without scales and continuous pith.

steps.title: 4 · Styrax flower and fruit
steps.look_for: Usually 5–6 corolla lobes, partly inferior ovary, and a globose non-winged capsule/nutlike fruit.
steps.why_it_matters: Reproductive architecture closes the genus split.

steps.title: 5 · Put all five differences on one card
steps.look_for: scaled/naked bud; chambered/continuous pith; old/current shoot flowers; fully/partly inferior ovary; winged/non-winged fruit.
steps.why_it_matters: High-retention visual comparison for crew training.

comparisons.title: Styracaceae vs Symplocaceae
comparisons.rule: Both are woody Ericales with inferior or partly inferior ovaries. Symplocaceae has very numerous epipetalous stamens and drupes with persistent calyx; Styracaceae project taxa have fewer stamens and dry fruits.

comparisons.title: Styracaceae vs Sapotaceae
comparisons.rule: Sapotaceae commonly has latex and fleshy fruit with a hard glossy seed; Styracaceae has dry capsular/nutlike or winged fruits and no latex-based project cue.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not reduce Styracaceae to 'white bell flowers'; use ovary and fruit architecture.

genera.fast_cue: scaled buds + chambered pith + 4-lobed flower + fully inferior ovary + winged fruit
naked buds + continuous pith + 5–6-lobed flower + partly inferior ovary + non-winged capsule

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted; FNA treats five subspecies, with Texas in the species range.

visual_targets.annotation_goal: bud, pith, shoot, ovary and fruit

curation_status.family_backfill_phase: recognition module built; species promotion independent
